papers.title_in_file: Photon Conversion and Interaction on Chip
papers.version_note: The file is the arXiv v1 preprint (2105.00275v1, dated May 4, 2021). Its title differs from the record id's wording (Quasi-Phase-Matched), but the content is the same device and experiment.

figures.shows: Comparison of state-of-the-art cavity frequency conversion with efficiency above 10%. Columns: material platform, structure, nonlinear process, loaded Q (x10^5), conversion efficiency by photon number, pump power, reference. Rows: Si3N4 microring FWM-BS 60% at 50 & 8 mW; Si3N4 microring DFWM 13% at 0.33 mW; AlN microring SFG 42% at 35 mW; PPLN microring SHG 10% at 0.3 mW; PPLN microring SHG 26% at 1.8 mW; PPLN millimeter disk SHG 18% at 9 mW; this work PPLN microring SFG 65% at 0.1 mW with Ql 1.3/1.3/2.6. The note explains why a 33% SHG preprint is excluded.
figures.confirmed_by: The state-of-the-art frequency conversion in χ(2) and χ(3) cavities

figures.shows: (a) Schematic of the Z-cut periodically poled microring with a pulley coupler. Pump ωp and signal ωs enter, SF light ωf exits. Insets show three resonances and the momentum bookkeeping mp, ms, M, mf. (b) SEM of the etched pulley coupler (1 µm scale bar). (c) SEM of the periodically poled microring (50 µm scale bar).
figures.confirmed_by: Schematic of the Z-cut periodically poled microring

figures.shows: (a) Transmission (dB, 0 to about -6) against detuning (pm) for three resonances (i) 1560.15 nm, (ii) 1551.85 nm, (iii) 778.00 nm. Dips are about 4 dB deep. Labelled Q values: (i) Ql 1.31e5, Qc 1.61e5, Q0 7.10e5; (ii) Ql 1.28e5, Qc 1.60e5, Q0 6.35e5; (iii) Ql 2.55e5, Qc 3.00e5, Q0 1.21e6. (b) Diagram of parametric processes (SFG, SHG, Raman, SPDC) and the band-pass filter at 778 nm. (c) Unfiltered optical spectrum (power in dBm against wavelength 800 to 1600 nm) with pump near 1560 nm, signal near 1552 nm, a weak SF peak near 778 nm and a residual SH peak near 780 nm. The insert zooms in on the SF band. On-chip powers: pump -13.8 dBm, signal -44.3 dBm, SF -44.0 dBm.
figures.confirmed_by: Original optical spectrum before any optical ﬁltering when strong pump and weak signal are applied.

figures.shows: Left axis: SFG efficiency ηQE (%, 0 to 100), red squares with a red fit curve. Right axis: noise photon flux (MHz, 0 to 2.5), black squares with a black fit curve. X axis: on-chip pump power (µW, 0 to about 220). ηQE rises steeply, peaks near 65% around 100 µW, then falls slightly. Noise rises superlinearly, fitted as P^2.4, reaching about 2.2 MHz at the highest pump power.
figures.confirmed_by: ηQE = 65% is obtained at the pump power around 100 µW.

figures.shows: ηQE (x10^-5, 0 to 2.5) against intracavity mean pump photon number (0 to about 2). Data points lie close to a straight red line through the origin. The yellow inset zooms to about 0.8 to 1 photons and shows ηQE of about 1 x 10^-5 at one photon.
figures.confirmed_by: Inset is an zoom-in to shown a quantum eﬀciency of ηQE = 10−5 is achieved at

figures.shows: Schematic of a proposed TFLN integrated chip for heralded entanglement generation. A PPLN waveguide makes SPDC pairs. Thermally tuned microring filters, a-Si cladding, directional couplers and a PPLN microring converter are shown, with a reference arm and channel labels ωs1, ωs2, ωi1, ωi2, ωs1+s2. It is a design illustration, not a measurement.
figures.confirmed_by: Illustration of a TFLN integrated photonic circuit for heralded entanglement generation.

figures.shows: Simulation parameters for the coupled-mode model. Dissipation rates (MHz x 2π): pump total 1467.9, intrinsic 270.8, coupling 1197.0; signal 1510.3, 304.4, 1205.9; SF 1512.2, 318.7, 1193.5. Effective nonlinear susceptibility 16.4 pm/V (Fig. 3) and 18.2 pm/V (Fig. 4). Effective mode area 1.0 µm^2, radius 80 µm, overlap factor 90%. Fitted g is 8.2 MHz for Fig. 3 and 9.1 MHz for Fig. 4.
figures.confirmed_by: The ﬁtted ga and gb are 8.2 MHz and 9.1 MHz, respectively.

figures.shows: Experimental setups. (a) Classical setup: telecom and visible lasers, polarization controllers, WDM modules, device under test on a thermoelectric cooler, photodetectors. (b) Quantum setup: pump and signal telecom lasers with VOAs and FPCs, 10%/90% taps to SNSPDs through attenuators, WDM, DUT on TEC, an OSA, and a free-space filtering system (collimators, short-pass, band-pass, narrow band-pass filters) feeding a Si single-photon detector.
figures.confirmed_by: Setups for classical (a) and quantum (b) experiments.

papers.what_it_is: An experimental paper reporting a periodically poled thin-film lithium niobate microring, triply resonant and strongly overcoupled, that reaches 65% sum-frequency conversion at about 100 µW pump power with low noise, and measures photon-level coupling (g of 9.1 MHz, about 10^-5 conversion per intracavity pump photon).

assertions.value: The authors report an external quantum efficiency of (65 ± 3)% with (104 ± 4) µW pump power in a periodically poled lithium niobate microring sum-frequency generation device.
quotes: The external quantum eﬃciency reaches (65 ± 3)% with only (104 ± 4) µW pump power
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-device empirical result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract says the efficiency improves the state of the art by over one order of magnitude, while the introduction says orders of magnitude. Table I lists 42% at 35 mW for the best prior SFG (AlN), so the gain is mainly in pump power.

assertions.value: The authors report that, accounting for all insertion losses on and off chip, the peak conversion corresponds to about 9% total efficiency.
quotes: Taking into account all insertion losses both on and oﬀ chip, this corresponds to about 9% total eﬃciency.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-device empirical result.
assertions.reader_inference: The gap between the on-chip 65% and the 9% total is set by fiber-chip coupling losses of about 8 dB and 9.5 dB and by other losses. The 65% headline is an on-chip figure.

assertions.value: The authors report an on-chip noise photon flux of 0.3 MHz under continuous-wave pumping at the 65% peak quantum efficiency.
quotes: At the 65% peak QE, the onchip noise photon ﬂux is 0.3 MHz under continuous-wave pumping.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-device measurement.

assertions.value: The authors state that if pulses of about 100 ps matching the cavity lifetime were used, the noise photon per pulse would be 3 × 10−5; this is a conversion from the continuous-wave flux, not a pulsed measurement.
assertions.anchor: Abstract, p.1; Low-noise Frequency Conversion, p.4
quotes: At the peak conversion, 3 × 10−5 noise photon is created during the cavity lifetime
If using ∼100 ps pulses that match the cavity lifetime, the noise photon per pulse is 3 × 10−5
assertions.certainty_reason: Derived from a CW measurement under an assumed pulse width.
assertions.reader_inference: 0.3 MHz times 100 ps gives 3 x 10^-5, so the per-pulse figure depends on the assumed 100 ps pulse width and was not measured with pulses.

assertions.value: The authors report that the noise photon flux grows between quadratically and cubically with pump power, fitted as the pump power to the power 2.4.
assertions.anchor: Low-noise Frequency Conversion, p.4; Figure 3 caption, p.5
quotes: the increase of the noise photon ﬂux is between quadratic and cubic with the pump power
Solid black line is ﬁtted to the pump power P as Nnoise ∼ P 2.4.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical fit from one device.

assertions.value: The authors state that the noise scaling indicates the cascaded SPDC and SFG process is present in addition to Raman scattering.
quotes: This result indicates that besides Raman scattering, the cascaded SPDC and SFG process also presents
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' interpretation of a scaling exponent; no separate measurement isolates the processes.

assertions.value: The authors state that the noise level can be substantially lowered by, for example, further detuning the pump from the signal.
quotes: This noise level can be substantially lowered by, for example, further detuning the pump from the signal [24].
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited expectation, not tested in this paper.

assertions.value: The authors report that fitting the classical efficiency data with the steady-state coupled-mode equations gives a photon-photon coupling coefficient g of 8.2 MHz.
quotes: g is determined to be 8.2 MHz
assertions.certainty_reason: Model fit with g as the single fitting parameter.

assertions.value: The authors report a normalized power transduction efficiency fitted to be about 4.5% per µW in the low conversion region.
quotes: the normalized power transduction eﬃciency is ﬁtted to be about 4.5% µW−1
assertions.certainty_reason: Fit to one device's data.

assertions.value: The authors report that fitting the single-photon-level data with the coupled-mode equations gives a photon-photon coupling coefficient g of 9.1 MHz, compared with 8.2 MHz from the classical measurement.
assertions.anchor: Interaction Between Photon-level Coherent States, p.5
quotes: to be 9.1 MHz, compared to 8.2 MHz as from the classical measurement
assertions.certainty_reason: Model fit to one data set.
assertions.reader_inference: Table S1 uses a different effective nonlinear susceptibility for each fit (16.4 and 18.2 pm/V). The ratio of the two g values (about 0.90) equals the ratio of these two values. The g difference may therefore reflect the model input rather than a physical change.

assertions.value: The authors suggest that the slightly higher g in the single-photon measurement may come from better QPM or triple resonance for single-photon light, due to the absence of thermo-optical and photorefractive effects.
assertions.anchor: Interaction Between Photon-level Coherent States, p.5
quotes: This slightly higher value may come from better QPM or triple resonance for single-photon light waves, due to the absence
assertions.certainty_reason: Speculative explanation, not tested.

assertions.value: The authors report an on-chip quantum efficiency of about 10−5 when there is one pump photon on average in the cavity, after correcting for coupling loss and finite detector efficiency.
assertions.anchor: Interaction Between Photon-level Coherent States, p.5
quotes: The on-chip quantum eﬃciency is about 10−5 when there is one pump photon on average in the cavity
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-device measurement with weak coherent states.
assertions.reader_inference: The pump is a weak coherent state, so one photon is a mean intracavity number, not a number-state input.

assertions.value: The authors state that the best efficiency reported hitherto for signal photon conversion with one pump photon in the cavity is 10−7, citing a prior work, versus about 10−5 here.
quotes: the external quantum eﬃciency for signal photon conversion is ∼ 10−5, while the best eﬃciency reported hitherto is 10−7 [20].
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' comparison to a cited prior result.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract's 'breaking the record by 100 times' follows from 10^-5 against 10^-7.

assertions.value: The authors report a linear dependence of the quantum efficiency on the intracavity pump photon number in the single-photon-level measurement.
assertions.anchor: Interaction Between Photon-level Coherent States, p.5
quotes: we observe linear dependency of the quantum eﬃciency on the intracavity pump photon number
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical observation, one device.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Figure 4 efficiencies have the 250 Hz detector dark counts subtracted and the 4.75 dB coupling loss and 50% detector efficiency accounted for.
quotes: Detector dark counts of 250 Hz have been subtracted
the coupling loss of 4.75 dB
assertions.certainty_reason: The caption states the corrections applied in the measurement setup.

assertions.value: The authors report a total detection efficiency for the sum-frequency photons of about 17%, from a detector efficiency of about 50% and a coupling efficiency of about 33.5%.
assertions.anchor: Interaction Between Photon-level Coherent States, p.5
quotes: the total detection eﬃciency for the sumfrequency photons is η = ηdηc ≈ 17%, with detector eﬃciency ηd ∼ 50% and coupling eﬃciency ηc ∼ 33.5%
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own detection setup parameters.

assertions.value: The authors report that with the signal blocked, even at the highest on-chip pump flux of about 5 GHz the photon counts remain at the dark count level of about 250 Hz.
assertions.anchor: Interaction Between Photon-level Coherent States, p.5
quotes: we block the signal and verify that even at the highest on-chip ﬂux (∼ 5 GHz), the photon counts remain at its dark count level (∼ 250 Hz)
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical control measurement.
assertions.reader_inference: This control addresses over-estimation of the single-photon nonlinearity by pump-induced background.

assertions.value: The authors report an internal Rabi rotation angle of 0.01 produced by a pump photon, computed from g of 9.1 × 10^6 and Qp,i of 7.1 × 10^5.
assertions.anchor: Interaction Between Photon-level Coherent States, p.5
quotes: In our case, g = 9.1 × 106 and Qp,i = 7.1 × 105, so that θ = 0.01
assertions.certainty_reason: Calculated from fitted g and measured Q.
assertions.reader_inference: Using the pump wavelength of 1560 nm, 2gQ/ωp gives about 0.011, consistent with the stated value.

assertions.value: The authors define the internal Rabi rotation angle as θ = 2gQp,i/ωp, which gives how much Rabi rotation a pump photon can induce while it is lost in the cavity.
assertions.anchor: Interaction Between Photon-level Coherent States, p.5
quotes: internal Rabi rotation angle θ = 2gQp,i/ωp
assertions.certainty_reason: Definition given in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that increasing θ to π/2 would require improving Qp,i to 108 (printed flat; read as ten to the eighth), which they say has been demonstrated in polished TFLN microdisks.
assertions.anchor: Interaction Between Photon-level Coherent States, p.5
quotes: Increasing θ to π/2 would require improving Qp,i to 108, which has been demonstrated in polished TFLN microdisks [18].
assertions.certainty_reason: Projection plus a cited demonstration.
assertions.reader_inference: This is a projection from a Q value shown in a different device, not demonstrated together with this conversion process.

assertions.value: The authors claim that, based on the current nonlinear parameters, a cavity quality factor of 108 (printed flat; read as ten to the eighth), which they say has been demonstrated in lithium niobate microdisks, will enable a C-NOT gate between single photons.
quotes: Based on the current nonlinear parameters, a cavity qualify factor of 108—which has been demonstrated in lithium niobate microdisks [18]—
will enable C-NOT gate between single photons.
assertions.certainty_reason: Forward-looking projection with no supporting calculation in this paper.
assertions.reader_inference: No gate fidelity or analysis is given; the device here has loaded Q of order 10^5.

assertions.value: The authors model sum-frequency generation by an effective Hamiltonian in which g is the photon-photon coupling strength, interpreted as the effective Rabi frequency produced by a pump photon.
quotes: the eﬀective Hamiltonian describing SFG between photons in their single modes is
g is the photon-photon coupling strength, which can be interpreted as the
Rabi frequency produced by a pump photon
assertions.certainty_reason: Definition of the model parameter.

assertions.value: The authors define the external quantum efficiency as the ratio of converted SF photons at the cavity output to input signal photons, so that internal cavity loss is accounted for.
quotes: Nf is that of converted SF photons at the cavity output (thus accounting for any internal cavity loss)
assertions.certainty_reason: Definition of the figure of merit.

assertions.value: The authors state that previous demonstrations used critical coupling, where most of the input power and about half of the converted photons are lost inside the cavity, and that for practical applications one needs to over-couple so photons are extracted before significant loss.
quotes: most of the input power and about half of the converted photons are lost inside the cavity
one instead needs to over-couple the cavity so that the photons can be extracted out
assertions.certainty_reason: Design rationale stated by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors state, citing a cited work, that under QPM and triple resonance the maximum quantum efficiency is approximately the product of the signal and SF ratios of loaded to coupling quality factor.
quotes: Under QPM and triple resonance (see Supplementary Material A), the maximum QE is given by [21]:
assertions.certainty_reason: Formula attributed to a cited work; the equation text layer is garbled, so only the sentence introducing it is quoted.
assertions.reader_inference: With the Q values in Figure 2 ((1.28/1.60) x (2.55/3.00)) the product is about 0.68, near the stated 65%.

assertions.value: The authors state that the measured Q factors give a highest possible external quantum efficiency of about 65%, and that an even higher efficiency requires further overcoupling.
quotes: give the highest possibl external quantum eﬃciency of ηQmEax ≈ 65%
For an even higher eﬃciency, the cavity needs to be further overcoupled.
assertions.certainty_reason: Calculation from measured Q's using a cited formula.
assertions.reader_inference: The measured peak of 65% matches this predicted ceiling.

assertions.value: The authors state that with a maximum quantum efficiency of about 65% and a normalized efficiency of about 4.5%/µW, the optimal pump power is around 115 µW.
quotes: In our case, ηQmEax ≈ 65% and ηtnroarn ≈ 4.5%/µW, so that the optimal power is around 115 µW.
assertions.certainty_reason: Calculation from fitted and measured parameters using a cited formula.
assertions.reader_inference: The measured peak at (104 ± 4) µW is close to this prediction.

assertions.value: The authors use a microring of 80 µm radius with a cross-section of 600 nm height and 1700 nm top width, with pump and signal in the telecom C-band and the SF in the visible band.
quotes: we use a microring with a radius of 80 µm and a cross-section of 600 nm in height and 1700 nm in top-width
The pump and signal are both in the telecom C-band and their SF is in the visible band
assertions.certainty_reason: Setup stated by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors state that all three waves are in fundamental quasi-TM modes interacting through the d33 tensor element with over 90% mode overlap, with mode numbers 602, 606 and 1357 and poling grating number M of 149.
quotes: all three waves are in the fundamental
through TFLN’s largest nonlinear tensor d33 with over 90% mode overlap
assertions.certainty_reason: Setup stated by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors select cavity modes at 1560.15 nm, 1551.85 nm and 778.00 nm, with the 1560.15 nm mode used as the pump to reduce the Raman background.
quotes: we select a set of cavity modes at 1560.15 nm, 1551.85 nm, and 778.00 nm
To reduce the Raman background, we designate the 1560.15 nm mode to the pump.
assertions.certainty_reason: Setup stated by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors set the pulley coupler top width by requiring npRp = nrRr, and use a top width of 400 nm, a gap of 650 nm and a length of 40 µm.
quotes: by requiring npRp = nrRr [22]
the pulley top width of wpulley = 400 nm, the gap of gpulley = 650 nm, and the length of Lpulley = 40 µm
assertions.certainty_reason: Fabrication parameters stated by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors report fiber-chip-fiber coupling losses of 8 ± 0.15 dB at 1556 nm and 9.5 ± 0.2 dB at 778 nm.
quotes: The ﬁber-chip-ﬁber coupling losses are measured to be 8 ± 0.15 dB at 1556 nm and 9.5 ± 0.2 dB at 778 nm, respectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: Measured device parameter.

assertions.value: The authors state that 430-nm of LN is etched leaving 170-nm, and that a concentric poling region with period 3.37 µm (M = 149, near 50% duty cycle) is made with several 1-ms and 450-V electrical pulses.
quotes: 430-nm thick LN is etched with 170-nm LN remaining
period of Λ = 3.37 µm given by Λ = 2πR/M , M = 149 and near 50% duty cycle
several 1-ms and 450-V electrical pulses
assertions.certainty_reason: Fabrication parameters stated by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors state that during measurement they optimize the temperature within 45 ± 0.3 °C and tune the lasers within ± 20 pm to compensate for phase mismatch and resonance drift caused by thermo-optical and photorefractive effects.
quotes: we only need to slightly optimize the temperature within 45 ± 0.3 ◦C
tune the wavelengths of both lasers within ± 20 pm
assertions.certainty_reason: Operating condition stated by the authors.
assertions.reader_inference: The device needs active temperature and wavelength tuning to hold triple resonance and QPM.

assertions.value: The authors fix the on-chip signal power at about 37 nW while the pump power is gradually increased in the classical efficiency measurement.
quotes: the signal power is ﬁxed to be about 37 nW on chip
assertions.certainty_reason: Setup stated by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors report that the unfiltered spectrum shows a low baseline except for a residual second-harmonic peak near 780 nm from the strong pump, and state that the low background shows other competing processes are well suppressed.
quotes: except for a residual second-harmonic peak at ∼780 nm by the strong pump
The otherwise low background over the entire spectral range shows that all other competing processes are well suppressed
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-device spectrum; the suppression claim is an interpretation of the spectrum.
assertions.reader_inference: The residual SH peak is removed with a ~3 nm bandpass filter, so the quantum-regime data depends on that filtering.

assertions.value: In the authors' comparison table of cavity frequency conversion with efficiency above 10%, the prior AlN SFG entry has 42% at 35 mW, a Si3N4 FWM-BS entry has 60% at 50 & 8 mW, and this work lists 65% at 0.1 mW.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' compilation of literature values and their own result.
assertions.reader_inference: The table counts only results with efficiency above 10%, a selection chosen by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors state that their 65% external efficiency with about 100 µW pump power marks orders of magnitude improvement over the state of the art across all existing photonic platforms.
quotes: marking orders of magnitude improvement over the state of the art across all existing photonic platforms
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' comparative claim.
assertions.reader_inference: Table I shows improvement in pump power by orders of magnitude relative to most entries but not in efficiency (42% to 65% for SFG). The abstract says over one order of magnitude, so the strength of the claim differs between sections.

assertions.value: The authors state that a recent preprint reporting 33% SHG efficiency is inconsistent with its own normalized efficiency of 602%/mW, since that would require a pump power several times larger than claimed, and they exclude it from the comparison table.
quotes: Note: a recent arxiv preprint reported
SHG of ηcon = 33% [18]. According to its reported normalized eﬃciency of 602%/mW, the required pump power shall be
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' criticism of another group's preprint.
assertions.reader_inference: The table note gives 1.75 mW as the required pump power and states it is over 16 times the claimed value, which is a critique of another group's numbers.

assertions.value: The authors present a design (not a fabricated or measured device) of an integrated chip for heralded entanglement generation, and state that with 12 pm filtering bandwidth and 100 ps pump pulses the heralding rate can approach 10 Hz for the demonstrated 10−5 conversion.
quotes: we present the design of
The heralding rate can approach 10
Hz for the demonstrated 10−5 photon conversion
assertions.certainty_reason: Projection for a proposed design; no heralding experiment is reported.
assertions.reader_inference: The heralding rate and the claim of orders-of-magnitude improvement over earlier heralded sources are estimates, not measurements on a built circuit.

assertions.value: The authors list effective nonlinear susceptibility values of 16.4 pm/V (used for the Figure 3 simulation) and 18.2 pm/V (used for the Figure 4 simulation) in the simulation parameters, with fitted g of 8.2 MHz and 9.1 MHz respectively.
quotes: eﬀective nonlinear susceptibility 16.4 pm/V
The ﬁtted ga and gb are 8.2 MHz and 9.1 MHz, respectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: Model inputs and fits for one device.
assertions.reader_inference: The ratio 16.4/18.2 is about 0.90, equal to 8.2/9.1, so the g difference between classical and single-photon fits tracks the different d_eff used in the two simulations.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that they demonstrated photon conversion and interaction with record high efficiency and low noise in a Z-cut periodically poled microring on thin-film lithium niobate, with 65% transduction at about 100 microwatt pump power.
quotes: We have demonstrated photon conversion and interaction with record high eﬃciency and low noise
we achieved 65% wavelength transduction with only about 100 microwatt pump power
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' summary conclusion of their results.

assertions.value: Read from Figure 3: the SFG efficiency rises steeply with on-chip pump power to a peak of about 65% near about 100 µW, then declines slightly to about 61% at about 210 µW. The noise photon flux stays near zero up to about 50 µW and rises to about 2.2 MHz at about 210 µW.
quotes: SFG eﬃciency ηQE (left-axis, red square) and the generated noise photon ﬂux Nnoise(right-axis, black square) plotted against the on-chip pump power.
assertions.certainty_reason: Values read by eye from a plot.
assertions.reader_inference: The efficiency drops at higher pump while noise grows faster than linearly, so there is a trade-off in pump power.

assertions.value: Read from Figure 4: ηQE rises from about 0.45 x 10^-5 at about 0.4 intracavity photons to about 1.7 x 10^-5 at about 1.75 photons, following a straight red line through the origin with slope of about 1 x 10^-5 per photon.
quotes: Quantum eﬃciency ηQE versus the intracavity mean pump photon number.
assertions.certainty_reason: Values read by eye from a plot.

assertions.value: Read from Figure 2: the three resonances show dips of about 4 dB, with labelled Q values about 1.31 x 10^5 loaded and about 7.10 x 10^5 intrinsic (pump mode), about 1.28 x 10^5 loaded and about 6.35 x 10^5 intrinsic (signal mode), and about 2.55 x 10^5 loaded and about 1.21 x 10^6 intrinsic (SF mode).
quotes: Optical spectra of the interacting TM00 cavity modes at (i) 1560.15 nm, (ii) 1551.85 nm, and (iii) 778.00 nm
assertions.certainty_reason: Values read from labels in a figure.
assertions.reader_inference: The pump intrinsic Q matches the Qp,i of 7.1 x 10^5 used for the Rabi angle; the loaded Qs match Table I's 1.3/1.3/2.6 x 10^5.
